paper_title: On the Approximability of the Traveling Salesman Problem with Line Neighborhoods
classifications: Theory of computation → Approximation algorithms analysis
statement: √ for d = O(log n): there is no ( 2 − ε)-approximation assuming P ̸= NP and no (2 − ϵ)- approximation assuming the UGC. On the positive side, we gave an O(log2 n)-approximation algorithm in slightly superpolynomial time. There is still a large gap between the lower bounds and the algorithms for TSPN with line neighborhoods. Perhaps the most important question related to TSPN is to find a constant-approximation for line neighborhoods in R3 , or to prove that it does not exist. Furthermore, for general point sets in higher dimensions there is an inapproximability of Ω(log2 n/(log log n)3/2 ) under the Projection Games Conjecture. Whether that holds for flats or lines is an open problem.
context: We have shown that TSPN with line neighborhoods is APX-hard, so a PTAS for this problem is unlikely. This implies the same hardness for k-dimensional flats in Rd for 1 ≤ k ≤ d − 2, which together with the known PTAS results for k = 0 and k = d − 1 gives a complete classification of these problems. We have also proved a stronger inapproximability factor √ for d = O(log n): there is no ( 2 − ε)-approximation assuming P ̸= NP and no (2 − ϵ)- approximation assuming the UGC. On the positive side, we gave an O(log2 n)-approximation algorithm in slightly superpolynomial time. Perhaps the most important question related to TSPN is to find a constant-approximation for line neighborhoods in R3 , or to prove that it does not exist. Furthermore, for general point sets in higher dimensions there is an inapproximability of Ω(log2 n/(log log n)3/2 ) under the Projection Games Conjecture. Whether that holds for flats or lines is an open problem.
